svg.title: Estimated time to break-even updates as evidence arrives
svg.desc: For the same cohort, the forecast shows how many days remain until break-even; negative values mean the estimated break-even date is already past. A second panel shows the separate probability of no break-even by age 425. Two equally priced fictional source worlds follow the same fixed cohort acquired on calendar day 70. At each cutoff the model is refit using only then-visible observations and predicts that cohort under hold-current future conditions. In the top panel, zero means break-even on the information cutoff day; positive values mean the forecast is still ahead, and negative values mean the model estimates break-even has already happened. For example, at cutoff day 119 the cohort is 49 days old; a forecast of 34 days after acquisition appears as −15 days from cutoff. The solid line is the median among predictive paths that cross zero by cohort age 425. Darker fill is the middle 50%, pale fill the middle 80%, and dashed lines show evaluator-only hidden outcomes. The lower panel reports predictive paths with no break-even by cohort age 425. These posterior predictive intervals need not shrink monotonically: new evidence can shift or widen the estimate, and future process variation remains. Both sources have the same $0.05 per-lead price; their hidden subscriber performance differs.
